headline: Reuse a candidate without repeating combinations
statement: Given distinct positive integers candidates and a positive target, return every combination whose values sum to target. A candidate may be chosen any number of times. Combination order and result order do not matter; no duplicate combinations are allowed.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
intuition: Build a combination by choosing numbers in increasing order. Subtract each choice from the amount still needed. You may choose the same number again, but do not return to smaller numbers. This finds each combination once instead of repeating it in different orders.
approach: Sort candidates and keep a path and remaining target.
From start onward, try each value no larger than the remainder.
Recurse with the same index to allow reuse; pop the value on return.
Save a copy when the remainder reaches zero.
correctness: Every path is nondecreasing, so permutations of one combination cannot produce duplicates. Any valid multiset can be written in that order and follows a permitted path. Positive values reduce the remainder, and stopping at zero saves exactly combinations totaling target.
bruteForce: List ordered sequences of candidates. This explores permutations of the same answer and requires deduplication afterward.

complexity.time: O(n log n + n^d * d), d = floor(target/min(candidates))
complexity.explanation: n is the number of candidates and d=floor(target/min(candidates)) is maximum path depth. Sorting costs O(n log n); at most n choices per depth give a conservative exponential search bound. Each saved result costs O(d) to copy. The sorted copy uses O(n), and path plus recursion use O(d), excluding output.

pitfalls: Reuse requires passing i, not i+1.
Save path[:] rather than the mutable path.
Positive candidates are essential for termination.
